subject.title: Runtime Self Context: give agents runtime, scale, offload, and cost awareness

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core runtimeContext config plus model-facing runtime tool as the v1 runtime self-awareness contract, narrow that first slice, or defer the design to plugin/provider extension work?
rationale: The request changes core config, prompt exposure, tool policy, session/context state, and provider/plugin ownership, so source inspection can show what is missing but cannot choose the intended product/API boundary.

options.title: Approve v1 core contract
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90101 as the first config-backed, non-mutating runtime self-context slice and track provider refresh, action execution, and precise cost estimation separately.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Limit the first slice to the smallest prompt/tool or environment-adapter contract maintainers are ready to support, leaving speculative fields out until provider hooks are designed.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API design
options.body: Keep the issue open as a design tracker and require a plugin/provider hook proposal before adding new core config or model-facing tool surface.

recommendation.title: Approve v1 core contract
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90101 as the first config-backed, non-mutating runtime self-context slice and track provider refresh, action execution, and precise cost estimation separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked PR explicitly asks this handle for feedback, and the unresolved question is product/API direction rather than implementation ownership.
